transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Um… yeah, thanks, doctor. I guess I’m here because I’ve been kind of stuck on how my face looks. It sounds stupid when I say it out loud, but the left side of my face just looks… crooked to me, like messed up somehow.

I know people tell me they don’t see anything, but when I’m at the warehouse, or even at salsa night, I feel like everyone’s noticing it. I try to tell myself it’s probably not as bad as I think, but I can’t really stop thinking about it.
Have you found yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to fix it in some way because of how your face looks?

Yeah… I mean, I do some of that. Not like, all day or anything… but before I go back out on the inventory floor, I’ll stop in the bathroom and check the mirror a few times. I’ll fix my cap, kind of rub at that same spot on my face, like maybe I can make it look more normal.

I know that probably sounds weird. I try not to take too long, but sometimes I get stuck doing it and then I’m late getting back, and my picking numbers fall behind. My boss has gotten on me about it more than once.

Does this concern about the left side of your face ever get in the way of your daily activities — like work, hobbies, or spending time with friends — or cause you a lot of distress even when others don’t seem to notice anything?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has been affecting stuff.

At work, I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed, like from checking or trying to get myself together before going back out. And outside of work… I’ve kind of stopped going to soccer sometimes, and I’ve skipped salsa nights too. Even family gatherings, if I think people might be looking at me or taking pictures, I’ll make an excuse not to go.

I know that probably sounds… not great. I’m trying not to let it run my life, but I guess it kind of is getting in the way.

Can you describe what goes through your mind when you look at your face in the mirror? Like, do you worry that others see you as unattractive, or do you feel like there’s something physically wrong or abnormal that needs to be fixed?

When I look in the mirror, I mostly get stuck on the left side of my face. It just looks crooked to me… like it’s not lined up right, or like something is messed up there.

I know people say they don’t notice it, and I don’t want to sound like I’m being dramatic, but it’s hard for me to believe them. My mind goes straight to, like, “Everyone can see this.” At work, at the warehouse, or if I’m at salsa night, I feel like people are noticing that side of my face even if they’re not saying anything.

I guess I worry it makes me look strange or off somehow. I know maybe that doesn’t make sense, but that’s what it feels like when I see it.
When you look at the left side of your face, do you believe that the way it looks is something that others would typically find noticeable or unattractive, even if they don’t mention it?

Yeah… I mean, I know people say they don’t see anything, and I’m trying to take that in, but when I look at it, it really does seem noticeable to me.

Like the left side just looks crooked or messed up somehow, and I start thinking, “There’s no way other people aren’t seeing this.” At the warehouse, or if I’m at salsa night, I’ll be thinking people are noticing it even if they’re being nice and not saying anything.

I know that probably sounds a little much… but yeah, I guess I do believe it looks off enough that people would notice.
Do you ever feel anxious or preoccupied about other parts of your body, or is your concern mostly focused on the left side of your face?

It’s mostly the left side of my face, yeah.

I mean, I don’t really sit there worrying about, like, my whole body or anything like that. It’s just that one area I get stuck on. I keep thinking it looks crooked or messed up, and then my mind goes to people at the warehouse or salsa night noticing it, even when they tell me they don’t see anything.

I know that might sound like I’m overdoing it, but… that’s the thing I can’t seem to stop thinking about.

When you check your face in the mirror or fix your cap, do you feel a need to do it a certain way or a certain number of times to feel reassured or to prevent something bad from happening, like people noticing your face more?

Yeah… I mean, not like a number exactly. I’m not counting it or anything.

But I do feel like I have to check it the right way before I go back out on the inventory floor. I’ll stop in the bathroom and look at that side of my face, fix my cap, rub at the same spot a little… just trying to make it look normal, I guess.

I know that probably sounds kind of stupid. I don’t think I’m preventing something terrible, exactly, but it feels like if I don’t get it right, people are going to notice it more. And sometimes I stay in there too long doing that, and then my picking numbers fall behind, and my boss gets on me again. I’m not trying to mess around at work, it’s just… I get stuck.

When you’re worried about how the left side of your face looks, do you find yourself doing anything else besides checking the mirror — like comparing it to how it looked before, analyzing it in your mind, or trying to hide it — to try to feel better or less anxious about it?

Yeah… I guess I do some of that, maybe not in a big dramatic way, but I’ll kind of get stuck on it.

Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I’ll go in the bathroom and check that side of my face in the mirror, fix my cap a certain way, and sometimes rub at that same spot like I’m trying to make it look normal. I know that probably sounds kind of… I don’t know, vain or weird, but it’s more like I’m trying to calm myself down before people see me again.

And sometimes I take longer than I mean to. Like, I’ll think I’m just going to check real quick, but then I’m late getting back, and my picking numbers fall behind, and my boss gets on me. I’m not trying to slack off or anything. I just kind of lose time with it.
When you check your face or adjust your cap, do you feel like you have to do it in a very specific way, or do it until it feels 'just right,' even if you can't explain why?

Yeah… I think it’s more like “until it feels right,” I guess. Not a number or anything.

Like before I go back out on the inventory floor, I’ll check that side of my face in the bathroom mirror, fix my cap, and rub at the same spot a little. I tell myself I’m just making sure it looks okay, but sometimes I keep doing it longer than I meant to.

And then I’m late getting back, my picking numbers fall behind, and my boss gets on me again. I know that probably sounds bad… I’m not trying to waste time. It just feels hard to walk back out until I’ve got it as okay as I can.
When you’re worried about how the left side of your face looks, is your main concern that people will judge you negatively or think poorly of you because of it?

Yeah… I think that’s pretty much it. I don’t want to sound like I’m assuming everyone’s staring at me, but that’s what it feels like.

Like, I get stuck thinking the left side of my face looks crooked or messed up, and then I’m worried people at the warehouse notice it, or people at salsa night notice it. Even when someone says they don’t see anything, I still feel like maybe they’re just being nice or they don’t want to say it.

So yeah… I guess I’m scared they’ll think I look weird or judge me for it.
